ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a waveform of sinusoidal voltage u varying with time t(ms), the vertical axis is labeled u(V), and the horizontal axis is labeled t(ms). The waveform reaches a negative peak at t≈0.5 ms, and the figure marks this valley value as -311 V with a dashed line; afterward the waveform rises and reaches a positive peak at t≈2.5 ms; it crosses the horizontal axis near t≈1.5 ms and t≈3.5 ms. Reasoning: From the negative peak value -311 V, the voltage maximum value is Um=311 V. From the valley at t=0.5 ms to the peak at t=2.5 ms, the interval is 2 ms, which is half a period, so T=4 ms=0.004 s. The angular frequency is ω=2π/T=2π/0.004=500π rad/s. Let u=311 sin(500πt+φ). At t=0.5 ms=0.0005 s, u=-311, so sin(500π×0.0005+φ)=-1, that is 500π×0.0005+φ=-π/2. Because 500π×0.0005=π/4, φ=-π/2-π/4=-3π/4. Therefore the analytic expression is u=311 sin(500πt-3π/4) V.

Therefore write u=311 sin(500πt-3π/4) V.
